title: Edmund and the Signal
premise: Emrys Iversen smuggles memories in sealed crystal vials through the decaying orbital station of Halvard's Reach, and alone maintains a beacon that broadcasts a false fleet-signature keeping two hostile armadas at bay. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a signal only they can hear—Emrys realizes the beacon is no longer transmitting his lie but something older, something alive beneath the ice of the moon below. As the truce clock runs down, Emrys, customs officer Sefa Kwan (his lover on the other side of the law), and the dream-children must choose between preserving the deception that keeps both fleets from firing and answering the genuine call rising from the moon. In the end Emrys lets the beacon die, the truth is broadcast, and the fleets—faced with a third presence neither can deny—stand down; the children keep the new signal alive, and Emrys finally stops running.
about_author: F. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who left academia to write about the people who live in the static between transmissions. They live off-grid with two cats and an unlicensed shortwave rig.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Emrys: a routine smuggling run past orbital customs introduces his trade in forbidden memories and his careful invisibility among Halvard's Reach's forgotten dockworkers. He quietly services the old beacon no one remembers commissioning. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence—the cost of being nobody to everyone.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream Alike
chapters.summary: POV Nia, a nine-year-old dockworker's daughter: she wakes reciting coordinates she shouldn't know, and finds eleven other children sharing the identical dream of a blue light under ice. Adults dismiss it as station fever. Emotional beat: eerie wonder curdling into fear as the children realize the dream knows their names.

chapters.title: Customs and Consequences
chapters.summary: POV Sefa Kwan, customs officer: she flags an anomaly in the beacon's power draw and traces it toward Emrys, her secret lover, forcing her to falsify her first report. Meanwhile fleet chatter hints the truce expires in forty days. Emotional beat: love pulling against duty, the first crack in Sefa's certainties.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Was For
chapters.summary: POV Emrys: digging into the beacon's origins, he learns it was built to mask the moon's own transmission—a genuine signal buried decades ago by the first colonists who feared what it would summon. The children's dream is the buried signal resurfacing. Emotional beat: dread of inheritance; his lie was built atop someone else's silence.

chapters.title: Forty Days
chapters.summary: POV rotating ensemble: the truce countdown becomes public; both fleets send advance scouts demanding proof of the 'neutral garrison' the beacon claims exists. Emrys scrambles to fabricate crew manifests and ship transponders. Emotional beat: escalating pressure, found family forming around the shared secret in the station's lower decks.

chapters.title: The Scout
chapters.summary: POV Sefa: a scout captain arrives, sharp-eyed and courteous, and Sefa must host him while hiding that the garrison is thirty dockworkers and twelve dreaming children. One child, Tomas, nearly tells him about the dream. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness intertwined; Sefa realizes she'd burn her career to protect them.

chapters.title: Under the Ice
chapters.summary: POV Emrys and Nia: following the children's map, Emrys descends to the moon's subsurface ocean and finds the source—an ancient alien relay still listening, patient, broadcasting not conquest but a question. Emotional beat: awe dissolving fear; the thing beneath the ice has been waiting to be answered, not obeyed.

chapters.title: The Lie Frays
chapters.summary: POV ensemble: the second fleet's scout arrives early and hostile; the fabricated garrison begins to unravel when a vial of contraband memory surfaces containing proof of the original cover-up. Sefa is suspended. Emrys and Sefa clash over whether to answer the relay or reinforce the lie. Emotional beat: betrayal, blame, and the raw honesty of two people out of safe ground.

chapters.title: Truce's End
chapters.summary: POV Emrys: with hours before the truce lapses, both fleets hold position weapons-hot, each waiting for the other to blink. Emrys makes his choice—he shuts down the beacon and lets the relay's true signal flood every channel, the children singing the response they've carried in their dreams. Emotional beat: sacrifice and surrender; giving up control to end the standoff.

chapters.title: Answered
chapters.summary: POV Nia, closing with Emrys: the fleets stand down, unable to fight over a question now asked of them all; negotiations begin with the relay as neutral ground. The station's forgotten people become its founding crew. Emrys, no longer invisible, stays—and Sefa stays with him. Emotional beat: quiet hope; survival redefined as something shared rather than hidden.
